Earnest night rules for carrier checks
The aim of this section is to explain the standard that applies

Companion Animal Travel Desk Carrier Check Standard

This section sets the everyday handling standard for pet travel documents, carrier review, and calm support at the desk. The Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps the process steady, clear, and kind so travelers and pets feel looked after from the first contact.

When a traveler arrives with a pet, the passenger coordinator confirms the booking details, checks the carrier for fit, ventilation, latch security, and clean condition, and explains any required travel steps in simple language. If a carrier needs attention, the coordinator should say so plainly and without blame, then help the traveler understand the next safe option. We expect prompt, respectful communication at every point, especially when a traveler is anxious or the pet seems unsettled.

If a concern is raised about cabin conditions, the coordinator logs the issue, keeps the tone calm, and routes the matter through the usual service path without delay. <<FACT F117>> The traveler should receive a clear response, and any follow-up note should stay factual, brief, and easy to track. If a claim involves delayed departure, the coordinator records the service note, confirms the support steps, and avoids promising anything beyond the approved process. <<FACT F109>> Supervisors listen carefully when a passenger is worried and help settle the case with patience and respect.

For any animal that shows signs of stress, the desk team should slow the conversation, reduce extra noise where possible, and focus on the safest practical plan for the pet and the traveler. The same applies whether the traveler is flying alone or with family support, and it applies to every route we serve. Clear notes, clean handoffs, and consistent judgment matter more than speed alone.

If anything about this standard is unclear, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
